item.title: UN says IMO confirms 25 seafarer deaths since Iran war began
item.description:
UN says IMO confirms 25 seafarer deaths since Iran war began

As many as 25 seafarers have been killed in 134 confirmed maritime incidents across the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East since the US and Israeli started war on Iran in February, according to Khalid Khiari, UN Assistant Secretary-General Khaled for the Middle East, Asia and the Pacific.

Briefing the UN Security Council on Friday, Khiari cited figures from the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) covering incidents recorded up to November 11.

He said October saw the highest monthly number of incidents involving commercial shipping since February, warning that continued disruption was driving up energy, transport and insurance costs and threatening global food security.

“This situation cannot be allowed to become the new normal,” Khiari said, calling for an immediate end to attacks on civilian vessels and the restoration of safe maritime navigation.

Bahrain’s representative told the meeting that about 1,600 vessels had been affected by disruptions in the waterway, leaving more than 23,000 seafarers stranded aboard their ships.

item.title: Mossad chief in Washington for talks on Iran, report says
item.description:
Mossad chief in Washington for talks on Iran, report says

Roman Gofman, chief of Israeli spy agency Mossad and one of Benjamin Netanyahu's closest confidants, was in Washington on Friday for talks with senior Trump administration officials about the war in Iran, Axios reported, citing three sources with knowledge of the matter.

 The visit comes as the Israeli prime minister is pressing President Trump to resume the war against Iran. Axios said Gofman was to meet CIA Director John Ratcliffe and later expected to travel to Miami to meet White House envoy Steve Witkoff.

Mossad, the CIA and the White House declined to comment, Axios said.

Meanwhile Israel's Channel 12 news reported that Gofman’s trip was not disclosed to Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot in his Thursday security briefing with Netanyahu.

Trump, who suffered a defeat in the midterm elections, has resisted the pressure to resume strikes on Iran. Also, on Friday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that further military action against Iran was unnecessary because the "economic pain" inflicted by the US sanctions on Tehran "was so great".

In a written statement, the Joint List said Jabareen hinted for the first time at unofficial contacts and negotiations with the opposition over how its lawmakers would vote on opposition proposals. The talks concern, among other issues, the Knesset speakership, repealing laws related to what the Joint List described as the “judicial overhaul,” and the formation of new parliamentary committees. item.title: 245 Palestinian children killed by Israeli forces in West Bank since October 2023, UN says
item.description: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said Friday that Israeli forces had killed 245 Palestinian children in the occupied West Bank since Oct. 7, 2023, including 41 in incidents involving reported stone-throwing. “The killing of a child is deplorable. The killing of a child for simply carrying or throwing stones is abhorrent,” Turk said. He stressed that international law required any use of force to be “necessary and proportional to the threat posed,” adding that violations must be subject to accountability. “There must be accountability for violations,” he said. item.title: Israeli attacks kill 6 Palestinians, injure around 20 in Gaza despite ceasefire
item.description: Six Palestinians were killed and around 20 others injured Friday in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip amid continued violations of a ceasefire agreement in effect since Oct. 10, 2025, according to medical sources and witnesses, Anadolu reports. In the latest attack, Israeli artillery shelling killed three Palestinians, including a woman and a child, and injured at least 10 others east of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, a medical source at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital said. Local sources and witnesses said Israeli forces fired several artillery shells toward the area, one of which struck an apartment in a residential tower. The shelling coincided with a nearby condolence gathering, triggering panic among civilians, the sources added. A Palestinian was also moderately injured […]

item.title: Israeli delegation to visit UAE Sunday in bid to restore flydubai flights to Tel Aviv
item.description: An official Israeli delegation is expected to visit the United Arab Emirates on Sunday in an attempt to restore flydubai flights to Tel Aviv, Israel’s Channel 12 reported Friday. The broadcaster said the delegation will seek to persuade Emirati officials to allow the airline’s flights to Tel Aviv to resume. According to Channel 12, flydubai’s suspension of flights to Tel Aviv remains in effect until Dec. 15. In late October, Channel 12 said flydubai had extended the suspension of its flights to and from Tel Aviv until Nov. 30, although the airline had not issued an announcement on the matter.
